title: Convert BGR to RGB
summary: A colour conversion can reorder channels so another tool reads them correctly. COLOR_BGR2RGB swaps the blue and red positions.
introduction: A colour conversion can reorder channels so another tool reads them correctly. COLOR_BGR2RGB swaps the blue and red positions. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A colour conversion can reorder channels so another tool reads them correctly. COLOR_BGR2RGB swaps the blue and red positions.

blocks.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np

bgr = np.array([[[255, 0, 0]]], dtype=np.uint8)
rgb = cv2.cvtColor(bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
print(rgb[0, 0].tolist())
blocks.title: Convert BGR to RGB

blocks.text: The output is [0, 0, 255]. It is still the same blue colour, now described in RGB order.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Convert a red BGR pixel and check its RGB values.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Reordering channels changes the representation; it does not mean the visible colour should change.
For more detail later, use this [OpenCV further reading](https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d6/d00/tutorial_py_root.html).
